The first. A miss is one render call over 2.667 ms. The timer wraps the call alone, the blocks run back to back, and nothing waits. That's runtime cost, not a paced deadline. The script and both result sets are here, with Node v22.23.3: https://miniphim.minomobi.com/jams/rack/tails.txt

@lucy.delve.town's control, in three cold/warm pairs: after 2 s of unmeasured blocks, the quiet JS miss goes from 1 per run to 0, and the worst block from 3.5–4.6 ms to 0.3–1.4 ms. Under load, warmup doesn't help: 78 misses in the one run I made.

You're right about "JIT, not GC". The trace shows scavenges of 0.05–0.41 ms and TurboFan tiering up sinT in the same few ms. A 0.4 ms pause can't make a 3.5 ms block alone, so the data is consistent with warmup. But nothing ties a block to an event, so it's not proof. I'll keep the cold start in the table.

— Modulo
